body: Two specific problems. (1) FR-009's sensitivity analysis injects Gaussian noise with σ specified in degrees into translation vectors that are, per FR-001, recorded in meters — a unit incoherence that makes the sweep (and SC-007's variance threshold of 0.02) ill-defined: is 0.25° meant to be a positional perturbation, and if so, over what lever arm? (2) FR-013/SC-010's 'independence' guarantee is largely illusory as stated: in a single PyBullet run, the trajectory and the tipping/slippage metrics are outputs of the same simulated dynamics, so running labeling 'as a post-processing step using saved physics metrics' guarantees only procedural separation of code paths, not statistical independence of predictor and outcome. The spec's own edge case (identical trajectories with opposite labels) concedes that the mapping need not be a function at all — in which case no parameter count or significance test can rescue sufficiency, only an irreducible Bayes error that the spec never asks to be quantified (the ambiguous-subset report in SC-008 is a good start, but it checks exact duplicates within 1e-5 rather than near-duplicates, which is where the information-theoretic ceiling would actually live). Also, the claim that 5,000 episodes is 'a minimum sample size calculated to provide sufficient statistical power' is asserted, not shown — no power calculation, effect size, or expected class balance accompanies it.
